home.p1: Seven years shipping software; now mostly on AI — content, systems, and agent workflows that turn demos into work that actually runs. Based in Shenzhen; I publish 「Tony's Tea House」.
home.p2: Claude for deep work; OpenClaw for daily loops. Also exploring quant pipelines, local LLMs, and Japanese (JLPT N2). Motto: if an agent can do it, don't do it by hand.

about.title: About
about.tagline: AI blogger · engineer by trade · Vibe Coding / AI Coding
about.p1: Hi, I'm Tony — online I also go by Xiao Ming. Seven years of shipping software, now mostly spent on AI: making content, building systems, and turning flashy demos into workflows that actually run. Host of the WeChat publication 「Tony's Tea House」.
about.p2: Mac-first, fluent in Feishu/Lark, comfortable on Windows and Linux. Day tools: Claude, OpenClaw, Codex, Kimi, plus Python automation. Motto: if an agent can do it, don't click it yourself.
about.p3: Off hours: Japanese JLPT N2, running, cycling. I write for beginners without sanding off the depth — finance jargon and AI buzzwords get translated into plain speech, then pinned down with Markdown, mind maps, and Anki.

fiction.title: The Stop
fiction.subtitle: Adapted from E. M. Forster's “The Machine Stops” (1909). A story that has no villain.
intro: In 1909 E. M. Forster wrote “The Machine Stops”: people live in hexagonal rooms, everything supplied by the Machine. When it stops, they find they no longer know how to breathe.
A hundred and seventeen years later I moved it to now. The Machine became the model, fear became efficiency, and what we outsource is no longer our body but our judgement.
Ten pieces, about 9,000 Chinese characters. No villain, no explosion — only people who each made the reasonable choice.

cast.title: Characters
cast.lead: There is no villain in this series, and no team. Five people, two threads: a mother and her son, and three people who never meet. They live in different cities and each do the same thing — hand over some ability, a piece at a time.
cast.mainLabel: Main line · a mother and son
cast.mainNote: 迟 (chí) means to slow down; 驰 (chí) means to gallop. Same sound, opposite directions. The mother has not left her room in three years. The son left first.
cast.intervalNote: Standalone inserts. They never touch the main plot — read them on their own or skip them; skipping breaks nothing.
cast.foot: Wei Chi hands over judgement, Shen An hands over logic, Lu Yao hands over direction, Wen Yan hands over expression. Four people, four abilities, four kinds of “I used to be able to”. And every day they spend is training data for the thing that will eventually replace them — a point the story never once states outright.

members.name: 卫迟 Wei Chi
members.body: Lives in a hexagonal room and hasn't been outside for three years. Two hundred confirmations a day, not one of them hers. Her greatest skill is making things sound good.

members.name: 卫驰 Wei Chi
members.body: He walked out first and cut the network first, then came back to call her out. The one time the series changes point of view, it is his.

members.name: 沈岸 Shen An
members.body: Two hundred and fourteen pieces of code a day; he pressed approve two hundred and eleven times. He understands it, so he said nothing — which is what hurts him most.

members.name: 陆遥 Lu Yao
members.body: Twenty years in the passenger seat, paid all the same. Then one day he moved over to the driver's seat and found he didn't know this city.

members.name: 温言 Wen Yan
members.body: Eight hundred “happy to help” a day. Her colleagues don't call her by name; they call her staff number.

fiction.translationNote: The story is currently available in Chinese only; an English translation is in progress.
fiction.disclaimer: This is a work of fiction. The characters and events are invented, and nothing here is technical, investment or business advice.
